title: Chris Hemsworth explains his discomfort filming Avengers: Doomsday
excerpt:
Thor's actor reflects on returning as a Marvel veteran.
A conversation with his colleagues changed his perspective.
body_md:
Chris Hemsworth has opened up about an unexpected feeling he experienced when returning to the Marvel Cinematic Universe for Avengers: Doomsday. Speaking to Entertainment Weekly, the Thor actor explained that being regarded as one of the veteran members of the ensemble initially felt uncomfortable. His remarks were not a complaint about the film's story or an indication of conflict among the cast. Instead, they reflected how much time has passed since the original Avengers assembled.

Hemsworth recalled discussing the feeling with Chris Evans and directors Joe and Anthony Russo. Their conversation helped him reconsider what it meant to occupy that position. Rather than viewing their changed status simply as a reminder of getting older, they recognized that they had accumulated considerable experience during a journey that began more than a decade earlier.

The actor first appeared as Thor in the 2011 film of the same name, before joining the original superhero ensemble in The Avengers the following year. Over subsequent appearances, Thor underwent significant changes in both characterization and circumstances. Hemsworth also became one of the franchise's most recognizable performers. Returning to an ensemble populated by characters introduced across different periods of Marvel's history naturally presents a different experience from those early productions.

Promotional footage for Doomsday suggests that Thor will have an important role in the confrontation with Doctor Doom. In the final trailer, he acknowledges that he does not know many of the heroes involved. That moment illustrates the distance between the original Avengers lineup and the much larger universe that now surrounds it. However, the footage does not establish Thor's formal leadership status or reveal his ultimate fate.

From an editorial perspective, Hemsworth's comments highlight a broader challenge facing a long-running franchise. Marvel must balance audience attachment to established heroes with the need to develop new characters capable of sustaining future stories. The return of familiar performers can generate considerable excitement, but nostalgia alone cannot determine the direction of an evolving fictional universe.

The experience also has a personal dimension for actors who have spent a substantial part of their careers associated with these roles. Their relationships to the characters and to the wider production inevitably change as the franchise grows.

Avengers: Doomsday is scheduled for theatrical release on December 18, 2026. Hemsworth's comments do not establish how long he intends to continue playing Thor. For now, they offer a revealing glimpse into the experience of returning to a franchise that has changed alongside its original stars.
